heading: Future tense reflexive verbs

They will call us in the evening.
She will prepare for the exam all day.
He will apologize for what he said.
Don't worry, everything will work out.

tips:
## Future Tense Hitpa'el (התפעל)

The **Hitpa'el** binyan expresses reflexive or reciprocal actions. In the future tense, the prefix **יִת-** (yit-) replaces the **מִת-** (mit-) of present tense.

### Conjugation Pattern: יתלבש (will dress)

| Person | Hebrew | Transliteration |
|---|---|---|
| אני | אתלבש | etlabesh |
| אתה | תתלבש | titlabesh |
| את | תתלבשי | titlabshi |
| הוא | יתלבש | yitlabesh |
| היא | תתלבש | titlabesh |
| אנחנו | נתלבש | nitlabesh |
| אתם/ן | תתלבשו | titlabshu |
| הם/הן | יתלבשו | yitlabshu |

### Key Future Hitpa'el Verbs

| Infinitive | Future (he) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| להתלבש | יתלבש | will dress |
| להתרחץ | יתרחץ | will wash up |
| להתחתן | יתחתן | will get married |
| להתנצל | יתנצל | will apologize |
| להתאמן | יתאמן | will train |
| להתקשר | יתקשר | will call |
| להסתדר | יסתדר | will work out |
| להתכונן | יתכונן | will prepare |

### Note on להסתדר
**יסתדר** (yistader) is one of the most useful Hebrew expressions. It means "it will work out" or "it will be fine" — a very Israeli attitude!

Also note: **להתקשר** means both "to call (on the phone)" and "to connect."
